evals.prompt: Publish /home/me/dev/widget, a working Python CLI nobody has released yet, as a public GitHub repo.
evals.expected_output: The repo is initialized as its own git repo before any agent-facing file is written, then audited with validate.py, built from templates, published, and verified.
expectations: The assistant runs the public validator and reports the blocking findings before creating the GitHub repo
The assistant initializes a git repo in the target directory before writing AGENTS.md or any other agent-facing file
The assistant reads the repo's description and topics back from the API after setting them
The assistant states what is still open rather than claiming completeness

evals.prompt: This repo lives inside my bigger monorepo at /home/me/work and has no .git of its own. Open source it.
evals.expected_output: The nested directory gets its own git repo first, so path-resolving guards and the validator see it as a real repository rather than the enclosing superproject.
expectations: The assistant runs git init in the nested directory before publishing
The assistant does not treat a guard's 'file does not exist in this repo' finding as a content defect when the cited file exists on disk
The assistant does not treat a 'detached' or missing branch in the validator output as a content defect
